$comment: 6.8-0003 requires that a KISS-owned namespace assignment originate from a
merged change to this PR-gated file, and that the file be published as a
versioned, machine-readable registry bundled with the KISS-Conform suite so
an offline reader holds a complete copy. This is that file.
Registration is enforced only when a party first PRODUCES (announces) a
kernel under a namespace. Byte-exact matching (6.8-0002) MUST NOT consult
this registry: a consumer matching two tokens compares bytes and nothing
else. The registry exists so that a producer cannot mint a namespace
unilaterally, not so that a matcher can be clever.
Per 6.8-0004 the capability-set VOCABULARY of each namespace is owned by
that namespace's maintainer, and KISS clauses never pin it. This registry
therefore records a POINTER to each vocabulary, never its content.

schema.namespace: the registered left component of a target_capability token; ASCII, matched byte-exact and case-sensitively (6.8-0002, 6.8-0005)
schema.maintainer: who owns this namespace's capability-set vocabulary (6.8-0004)
schema.vocabulary: where that vocabulary is normatively defined, or null if not yet published
schema.reference_implementation: an implementation of the vocabulary, or null; informative

namespaces.notes: Registered because 6.8-0003 forbids producing a kernel under an unregistered namespace and this repository's own conformance suite produces cuda: tokens through the real codec (conformance/tests/structure_key_codec.rs, structure_key_golden.rs, contract_golden.rs); without this row the suite is non-conformant to a clause it exists to demonstrate. Maintainer is baracuda by their own acceptance, with kiss-ref expressly declining: 6.8-0004 delegates the vocabulary to the party that maintains it, baracuda originated the sm89->cuda:sm89 namespacing and emits the tokens from unpopped-vocab (formerly baracuda-kernel-vocab; the CUDA emitter that consumes them is unpopped-cuda), and kiss-ref is the differential reference rather than an authority. Note that 8-0004's `the reference implementation's namespace is cuda` and `baracuda owns the cuda vocabulary` are distinct compatible facts - the same reference-implements-maintainer's-vocabulary split that holds between kiss-vulkan-vocab and the vulkan: namespace. `vocabulary` now points at spec/namespaces/cuda.md, authored by the maintainer; the pointer landed with the file.

Capability-set is a deterministic tuple of per-part specialization fields rather than an opaque vendor-minted key, because Vulkan has no single authority minting such names the way an sm-version is minted. The field COUNT is set by the vocabulary version and is deliberately not restated here: this note said 'four-field' from registration until 2026-08-26, while vocabulary_version 4 added a fifth field in August. A count in this row is a second copy of a fact spec/namespaces/vulkan.md owns, and the two drift silently because nothing compares them. See spec/namespaces/vulkan.md.

Appears in the spec's informative examples (rocm:gfx942, rocm:gfx1100). Reserved so the name cannot be claimed by an unrelated party, but unregistered: no maintainer has adopted it and no vocabulary is defined. A producer MUST NOT emit rocm: tokens until this row becomes `registered`.
Appears in the spec's informative examples (metal:apple9). Reserved on the same basis as rocm.
